what_happened: The the person running Athena closed by hand a stale queued request to pin a second study system. Admission refused it every time because it named a split file, and it blocked about 40 items behind it. The the person running Athena also added Sri's 4–8 November direction to the brief and set the focus to the study. Sri approved this after a clean-room review. No job failed and no gate ended anything.
cause: Queued items are written against the repo state at the time they are filed. Nothing revalidates them when that state changes, here a file was split. Nothing retires an item that is refused repeatedly. A single stale item therefore holds up the whole queue behind it until a person notices. The the person running Athena's own words say the follow-through loop that should catch stale blockers does not exist yet.
prevention: Add a follow-through step to the queue. When an item is refused for the same reason a set number of times (for example 3), it is moved aside with the reason recorded, so it stops blocking the drain. It is also re-checked against current repo state (named files still exist) and surfaced to the owner for close or rewrite. Items behind it then keep running without an the person running Athena closing the stale one by hand.
proposed_request: Add a follow-through step to the queue drain that retires stale blockers. (1) When a queued item is refused at admission for the same reason on 3 consecutive drain attempts, set it aside as "held-stale", record the refusal reason, and let the drain continue with the next items. (2) Before dispatch, check that every file or path the item names exists in the current repo; if not, hold the item with that reason. (3) List held-stale items on the owner's decisions page with the question to answer (close, rewrite or keep), not file paths. Acceptance: a test queues one item naming a nonexistent file ahead of three valid items and shows the three valid items run and the stale one is held with its reason recorded; a test shows an item refused twice is not yet held, and refused three times is held.
